subject.title: Browser tool: 7 improvements from real-world automation field test

question: Which remaining browser automation slice should OpenClaw core own next after selector targeting, selector waits, ARIA refs, and lower-level batch execution are already present?
rationale: The remaining asks change the browser tool's model-facing contract and state/debug signaling, so automation should not choose the API shape or bundle all seven improvements without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor one focused API slice
options.body: Pick one remaining behavior, such as model-facing batch exposure, stale-ref/readiness hints, CAPTCHA signaling, or element inspection, and require a narrow PR with live proof.

options.title: Keep as umbrella only
options.body: Leave this issue open as field-report context while narrower issues track each implementable browser behavior.

options.title: Defer new core surface
options.body: Keep current selector/wait/skill guidance and decline new browser tool signals until a maintainer validates stronger live traces.

recommendation.title: Sponsor one focused API slice
recommendation.body: Pick one remaining behavior, such as model-facing batch exposure, stale-ref/readiness hints, CAPTCHA signaling, or element inspection, and require a narrow PR with live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the partial implementation and have the clearest recent history on the selector/batch/browser act surface.
